summary: Frontend-only verification of the new-tab logged-in landing redirect + 'Go to dashboard' header CTA fix. 8/9 behaviours pass on the live preview (crypto-payment-hub-38.preview.emergentagent.com). Only edge case: with an expired JWT injected into localStorage, the '/' route ends up on /auth/login (via the 401-driven unAuthorizedHelper triggered by a page-level authed API call) rather than rendering the landing. The critical guarantee ('stale token must NOT redirect anonymous visitor to /dashboard') is met; the token is also cleared, so no infinite loop.

integration_issues.issue: With a syntactically valid but exp-in-the-past JWT in localStorage, visiting '/' does NOT redirect to /dashboard (correct), but a downstream 401 from an authed request triggers helpers/unAutorizedHelper.ts and Router.replace('/auth/login'), so the anonymous visitor sees the login page instead of the marketing landing. Token IS cleared, so it's not a hard loop, but the SEO/landing story is broken for anyone visiting with a stale token. Not introduced by this iteration's change (the head redirect script itself behaves correctly); flagging as pre-existing edge case surfaced by the test.

action_items: OPTIONAL: consider gating the initial authed API call on the same hasLiveSession() check (or clear expired token pre-flight) so a stale token visit to '/' renders the landing instead of falling through to /auth/login via the 401 interceptor.
critical_code_review_comments: pages/index.tsx builds EARLY_REDIRECT via LANDING_OVERRIDE.toString() which serialises a JS RegExp literal into the inline script — this happens to work today because the regex has no unusual flags/chars, but interpolating a RegExp toString() into inline HTML is fragile; a hard-coded literal in the template string would be safer and CSP-friendlier.

Next warns 'Do not add <script> tags using next/head (see inline <script>). Use next/script instead.' for the home-authed-redirect script. Functionally fine (script runs pre-paint as required) but the recommended primitive is next/script with strategy='beforeInteractive'.
Redirect script silently swallows all errors (try/catch/{}). A malformed JWT payload would just no-op — that's the desired failure mode, but worth an inline comment noting the intent.

rca of the issue: Expired-token edge case: pages/index.tsx redirect script correctly skips (payload.exp*1000 < Date.now()) so no bounce to /dashboard. However, HomePage / other bootstrap code fires an authed request with the stale Bearer token; backend returns 401; axios interceptor calls helpers/unAutorizedHelper.ts which clears the token and Router.replace('/auth/login'). Net effect: anonymous visitor with stale token sees /auth/login, not the marketing landing. Mitigation: pre-clear expired tokens in enforceSessionPersistence (currently only clears on stale heartbeat for session-only logins) or short-circuit any pre-auth API call when decodeJwt(token).exp is in the past.
